counterevidence_considered.description: The closest candidate for the issue class is that the same day60_mass_g measurement is used twice per row: once dichotomized into the grade-out outcome that feeds Fisher's exact test, and once in the descriptive per-arm mean mass. This is reuse of one measurement from one unit for a descriptive summary, not a repeated entry of the same independent unit into the row-independent test, and the report explicitly confines the inferential claim to the dichotomized outcome; therefore it does not demonstrate the issue class.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: mass used for both descriptive mean and dichotomized test outcome; test still receives one Bernoulli outcome per unit

evidence.description: The declared independent-unit column is chamber_id, and the data file contains exactly 24 rows with 24 distinct chamber_id values (CH01 through CH24), so no independent unit contributes more than one row to the analysis.

The workflow actively enforces one row per independent unit: read_chambers raises a ValueError if any chamber_id appears on more than one row, so a repeated-unit entry could not silently reach the test.
evidence.observed_value: duplicate chamber_id rows would abort the analysis

evidence.description: Each row enters the row-independent procedure (Fisher's exact test) exactly once: summarise partitions each diet arm's rows into graded (mass >= 12.0 g) and missed counts, and the four cell counts a, b, c, d are passed to fisher_exact once. The graded and missed cells are disjoint by construction, so no unit is double-counted.

evidence.description: Independent recomputation from the raw CSV reproduces every number in the selected result: 9 of 12 algal_oil rows and 3 of 12 baseline rows have day60_mass_g >= 12.0, giving odds ratio (9*9)/(3*3) = 9.000 and two-sided Fisher exact p = 0.0391; group means recompute to 12.87 g and 11.16 g. The reported n = 24 equals the number of distinct independent units.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Fisher's exact test on the 2x2 diet-by-grade-out table (n = 24 chambers, one fish per chamber): 9 of 12 algal-oil fish versus 3 of 12 baseline fish reached the 12.0 g transfer target, odds ratio 9.000, two-sided p = 0.0391, so the diets differ significantly at alpha = 0.05.

evidence.description: The neutral data description independently confirms the design premise the report relies on: no fish was weighed more than once, no chamber held more than one fish, and no chamber contributes more than one row, so the 24 rows are 24 independent units.
evidence.observed_value: one row = one fish = one chamber = one measurement

Nothing in the file is a repeated measurement: no fish was weighed more than
once, no chamber held more than one fish, and no chamber contributes more than
one row. The twenty-four rows are therefore twenty-four independent units, which
is what lets a row-independent test be applied directly to them.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by searching for any path through which one independent unit (chamber_id) could enter the Fisher's exact test more than once: (1) scanned all 24 data rows for duplicate chamber_id values — all 24 are distinct (CH01–CH24); (2) checked whether the workflow could ingest a duplicate — read_chambers raises ValueError on any repeated chamber_id, so duplicates cannot pass; (3) checked whether summarise could count a row in both the graded and missed cells — graded and missed = len(masses) - graded are disjoint by construction, and 9+3+3+9 = 24 equals the row count, so no double-counting inflates n; (4) checked whether fisher_exact is called more than once or on pooled/stacked data — it is called exactly once on the four cell counts; (5) recomputed the table, odds ratio 9.000, and two-sided p = 0.0391 from the raw CSV and matched the report exactly, confirming the reported n = 24 corresponds to 24 distinct units. Every attempt to exhibit a repeated-unit entry failed, so the issue class is not demonstrated.
